topic: How the sailing stones of Death Valley move
hook: In a dry lake in Death Valley, rocks move on their own.

scenes.narration: The lake bed is called Racetrack Playa. Scattered across it are heavy stones. Behind each one runs a long track, carved into the cracked mud.
Some of these stones weigh more than 300 kilograms. Yet nobody had ever seen one move.
For decades, people guessed. Strong winds. Strange magnetic fields. Even pranksters, sneaking out at night.
In 2013, a team of scientists set up cameras and weather stations on the playa, and waited.
That winter, they finally saw it. A thin sheet of ice formed on a shallow pond. Then the sun broke it into floating panels.
Light wind pushed the ice, and the ice pushed the stones. They crept along at two to five metres a minute.
No aliens. No magnets. Just ice, wind and patience.

loop_line: So next time you see a rock in the desert, look closely. It may be waiting for winter, ready to move on its own.
title: The sailing stones of Death Valley, solved
